title: Tool Use and Function Calling
description: Implement robust tool-calling loops with parameter binding, execution, observation, and retry behavior in C#.

blocks.text: Tool calling turns backend operations into model-invocable functions. A robust implementation handles parameter binding, validation, execution, observation, retries, and graceful degradation when a tool is unavailable or returns an error.

blocks.title: Typical loop
items: Model requests a tool with typed arguments.
Tool executes and returns structured output.
Model observes the result and decides whether to call another tool or answer.
Loop repeats until completion or a stop condition.

blocks.title: Tool-calling loop with AgentState and ToolExecutor
blocks.content: Complete tool-calling loop implementation including state management, tool execution, error handling, and sample conversation.

blocks.title: Watch for runaway loops
blocks.text: Set a maximum tool-call count per request. Unconstrained loops increase cost, latency, and failure surface.

items.text: I can trace a tool-calling loop end to end
items.hint: Request, validation, execution, observation, and next decision

items.text: I enforce a maximum number of tool calls
items.hint: Use a configurable limit to prevent runaway loops

items.text: I handle tool failures without crashing the agent
items.hint: Return structured errors and let the model decide how to proceed

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Tool calling is a loop, not a single call.
Validate arguments, handle errors, and bound execution.
Clear tool descriptions improve model behavior more than complex orchestration.
blocks.takeaway: Invest in tool descriptions and validation first. The loop will be more reliable when tools are easy to use correctly.
